_source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks, or The Bon-Vivant's Companion (New York: Dick & Fitzgerald, 1862). Public domain. Transcribed from the archive.org scan (howtomixdrinkso00schugoog), recipes 106-117.
_notes: Period measures modernized: wine-glass = 60 ml, pony = 30 ml, teaspoon = 5 ml, tablespoon = 15 ml. 'Bogart's bitters' in the scan is Boker's bitters; mapped to Angostura aromatic bitters with a note. Gum (gomme) syrup mapped to simple syrup with a note.

collection.name: Thomas 1862
collection.description: The cocktail chapter of Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862) — the first bartender's guide ever published. The cocktail as it existed before vermouth: spirit, bitters, sugar, curaçao.

recipe.name: Brandy Cocktail (1862)
recipe.instructions: Add the syrup, bitters, brandy and curaçao to a small bar glass. Squeeze lemon peel; fill one-third full of ice, and stir with a spoon.
recipe.description: № 107 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). "The 'Cocktail' is a modern invention, and is generally used on fishing and other sporting parties, although some patients insist that it is good in the morning as a tonic."
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 107

recipe.name: Whiskey Cocktail (1862)
recipe.instructions: Add the syrup, bitters and whiskey to a small bar glass with a piece of lemon peel. Fill one-third full of fine ice; shake and strain into a fancy red wine-glass.
recipe.description: № 109 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). The drink that would later take on ice and a muddled cube and become the Old Fashioned.
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 109

recipe.name: Gin Cocktail (1862)
recipe.instructions: Add the syrup, bitters, gin and curaçao to a small bar glass with a small piece of lemon peel. Fill one-third full of fine ice; shake well, and strain into a glass.
recipe.description: № 111 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). Gin in 1862 meant Old Tom or Holland gin — this predates the London dry style.
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 111

ingredients.note: Old Tom or Holland gin in period

recipe.name: Champagne Cocktail (1862)
recipe.instructions: Put the sugar, bitters and lemon peel in a tumbler. Fill one-third full of broken ice, and fill the balance with wine. Shake well and serve.
recipe.description: № 110 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). One bottle of wine to every six large glasses.
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 110

recipe.name: Japanese Cocktail (1862)
recipe.instructions: Add the orgeat, bitters and brandy to a tumbler with one or two pieces of lemon peel. Fill the tumbler one-third with ice, and stir well with a spoon.
recipe.description: № 113 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). Nothing Japanese in the glass — likely named for the first Japanese diplomatic mission's 1860 visit to New York.
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 113

ingredients.note: Half a teaspoonful of Boker's in the original

recipe.name: Jersey Cocktail (1862)
recipe.instructions: Put the sugar and bitters in a tumbler. Fill the tumbler with cider, and mix well, with lemon peel on top.
recipe.description: № 114 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). The cocktail formula applied to hard cider — no spirit at all.
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 114

recipe.name: Brandy Crusta (1862)
recipe.instructions: Mix the ingredients in a small tumbler with a little lemon juice and a small lump of ice. Take a fancy red wine-glass, rub a sliced lemon around the rim and dip it in pulverized white sugar. Pare half a lemon in one piece so the paring fits in the wine-glass, and strain the crusta from the tumbler into it. Then smile.
recipe.description: № 116 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862). "The 'Crusta' is an improvement on the 'Cocktail,' and is said to have been invented by Santina, a celebrated Spanish caterer." The sugared rim and citrus made it the ancestor of the Sidecar and the entire sour-with-liqueur line. The closing instruction is Thomas's own.
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 116
recipe.garnish: Sugared rim; the paring of half a lemon in one piece

recipe.name: Whiskey Crusta (1862)
recipe.instructions: Made the same as the Brandy Crusta, using whiskey instead of brandy: mix with a little lemon juice and a small lump of ice, and strain into a wine-glass rimmed with sugar and lined with a lemon paring.
recipe.description: № 117 in Jerry Thomas's How to Mix Drinks (1862).
recipe.source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862), № 117
recipe.garnish: Sugared rim; the paring of half a lemon in one piece
